messages: Lina: Quick UX question — the inline quota error that shows under the token meter reads: "Quota exceeded. Pause requests or upgrade." Screenshot + figma link: https://www.figma.com/file/xxx (see right of meter). Thinking we should soften and add a help link. Thoughts? Jon: I like softening. Maybe: "You've hit your monthly quota. Pause or request more capacity." Kyle: Avoid 'upgrade' as primary CTA for accessibility/enterprise customers. Also watch truncation on narrow screens — the current message wraps to 3 lines and looks noisy. Aisha: +1 to avoid 'upgrade'. How about two-tier copy: short inline, expanded on hover/tooltip. Inline: "Quota reached — requests paused." Tooltip: "You can request a quota increase or pause background jobs. See billing options." Marco: Tooltip sounds good. For the inline CTA label consider: "Request capacity" or "Request increase" (short). Lina: Nice. For the inline we need a concise phrase under 30 chars for mobile. "Quota reached — requests paused." is 34 chars incl spaces. Any tighter variants? Jon: How about "Quota reached — requests paused." -> "Quota reached — requests paused" (drop punctuation) still long. Kyle: Try: "Quota reached — paused" (weird). Maybe "Requests paused — quota hit" (still odd). Aisha: I'd prioritize clarity over exact char counts. Mobile can show "Quota reached" as primary and the CTA next to it: "Request capacity". So two elements instead of one long sentence. Marco: Agree. Also accessibility note: tooltip should be reachable by keyboard and announced by screen readers. Suggest adding aria attributes: role="status" aria-live="polite" for the inline state and aria-describedby for the CTA. Example snippet: ```html Quota reached Request capacity You can request a capacity increase or pause background jobs. Contact support for enterprise plans. ``` Lina: Great snippet, Marco. Should the CTA go to billing or to a support form? We have enterprise cases that need manual review. Jon: Link to a small modal that offers two paths: "Request capacity" (pre-filled form) and "Contact sales" for enterprise. We can deep-link from CTA to modal. Keeps copy generic. Kyle: Also add analytics events: `quota_inline_shown`, `quota_cta_clicked` with plan_id, so PMs can see friction. Aisha: Tone nit — avoid "quota hit" or "exceeded" words that sound punitive. Use "quota reached" or "quota limit reached". Also prefer sentence case: "Quota reached" not ALL CAPS. Lina: OK final proposal for mocks: Inline primary: "Quota reached" (bold) Secondary CTA: "Request capacity" Tooltip text: "You can request a capacity increase or pause background jobs. Visit billing or contact support." Accessibility: add aria-live and visually-hidden helper. Behavior: CTA opens modal with Request/Contact paths. Marco: LGTM. Small copy variants for QA: "Request capacity" vs "Request increase" — pick one after user testing but default to "Request capacity". Jon: I'll update the figma annotations and add copy tokens. designbot: lint-check: copy length OK (< 40 chars inline), tooltip length OK. No blocked issues. :white_check_mark: Lina: Thanks everyone. I'll push the updated mock now and add the accessibility snippet to the component README.
